hook.description: Cold open in a kitchen: the wife, mid-chore drying a bowl, turns to her husband (seated at the table, eyes fixed on his phone) and snaps 'Do you even listen to me?' He answers 'Yes' instantly and flatly, still not looking up from the phone.
hook.why_it_works: Opens on a universally recognizable domestic friction point (partner ignoring you for their phone) with a direct accusatory line of dialogue in the first second, plus the instant, too-quick 'Yes' signals to the viewer he's lying before any punchline lands -- creating immediate curiosity about how he'll get caught.

setup.description: The wife presses further, testing him with 'What did I just say?' -- the classic trap question that raises the stakes and sets up the reveal of whether he was actually listening.

conflict.description: A held beat of silence: the camera cuts in tight on the husband's face (glasses, phone still in hand), his expression blank and stalling, visibly scrambling for an answer with no dialogue at all -- the awkward pause is the conflict, dramatizing that he has nothing.

punchline.description: He finally answers with a vague, non-committal guess: 'Something went wrong. And there's a strong chance it's my fault.' It is a generic, deflecting non-answer that could apply to literally anything -- confirming he wasn't listening at all, and using self-deprecating vagueness as a coping mechanism instead of admitting it.

ending.description: No further dialogue or reaction shot from the wife is shown; the scene holds on the kitchen frame and then cuts to a plain black card, both stamped with the show's title treatment.
ending.cta_or_text_overlay: LOW BATTERY PEOPLE / CREATED BY NIN.
